label: copy-phase z input, strongest when followed by t
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost always (97% of mass) when the fed-back input is z; never in the original or delimiter phases, and essentially never on other inputs (a small t-input tail, 3% of mass, typically on the t right after a z t pair). Magnitude is set by what follows z in the original: the top activations (~0.9 of max) are z immediately followed by t (often z t t), with out_tok == t holding 62% of mass; z followed by a t one step later is next. z that is the first original token (recall_idx 1) is mostly inactive, and peak activity is at recall_idx 2-4. Plain copy-phase z covers 97% of mass but has only 8% precision, since most z inputs not followed by t are silent or only weakly active (<0.2 of max). The chosen predicate (z input, not first, with t output now or next) gets ~0.74 precision and ~0.70 mass recall on dev; the diffuse weak activation on other z contexts is what it misses.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+8.98), in_tok=z (+4.19), phase=2 & in_tok=t (+3.95), phase=2 & out_tok=t (+3.62), out_tok=t (+3.38), next_out=t (+3.18). Lower it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=z (-4.04), out_tok=n (-3.38), next_out=l (-2.75), phase=2 & out_tok=f (-2.73).
